Lenovo challenges MacBook Neo with colorful new laptop IdeaPad Vibe.

Lenovo's IdeaPad Vibe was unveiled at the company's Lenovo Innovation World event ahead of IFA, and it's clearly gunning for Apple's cheapest and wildly popular MacBook Neo—and it looks like it might actually be able to compete on specs. This laptop can be configured with a 14-inch or 15-inch OLED display, measures 14.9mm thick, and weighs in at just 2.87 lbs at its lightest. The chassis is a bit thicker and larger than Apple's laptop, but at least at the lowest weight, it's not far off. Lenovo says the Vibe will come in both plastic and metal body options.

However, the design is clearly pulling its weight, as Lenovo has teamed up with Pantone to offer the IdeaPad Vibe in seven different colors, including:

Dreamy Violet: A subtle purple shade with alluring layers, radiating tranquility for comfort wherever you go. Spicy Gold: A rich golden hue blending warmth and vibrancy for a confident, inviting feel. Zen Green: A nature-inspired green that evokes balance and harmony, encouraging you to slow down. Chill Blue: An icy blue paired with fresh, modern style for crisp clarity and an easy energy of starting fresh. Radiant Coral: Warm and uplifting with optimistic orange notes, bringing friendliness and positive energy wherever it goes. Moody Blue: A deep blue tone that conveys dependability and confidence, exuding refined elegance. Lowkey Grey: A timeless grey that exudes power, stability, and understated luxury.

The keyboard also features swappable keycap designs so you can mix and match for fun color combinations.

But pretty colors aside, Lenovo has packed this laptop with a pretty compelling configuration. There are two USB-A ports, an HDMI port, two USB-C ports, a headphone jack, and even a microSD card reader. There's also a 5-megapixel webcam (with a physical privacy cover), an optional keyboard backlight, and the 15-inch model can be configured with a touchscreen.

But what's under the hood?

You can choose between an AMD Ryzen AI 400 chip or a Qualcomm Snapdragon X chip. The AMD model supports up to 32GB of RAM, which users can upgrade themselves. The configuration also includes up to 1TB of storage, which is likewise upgradeable and has dual slots. The Snapdragon version supports up to 24GB of RAM and also has upgradeable storage, but the RAM is not user-upgradeable. Lenovo says an Intel version will be coming later.

The Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe will launch in two waves. The AMD model will go on sale in October, followed by the Snapdragon version in November. Both start at the same price of $699.99, which matches the MacBook Neo's new pricing after Apple's RAM upgrade.

Additionally, Lenovo has launched the IdeaCentre AIO I desktop all-in-one, available with a 24-inch or 27-inch display and similar color options to the Vibe, starting at $939 and also shipping in November.
